text: Hi! I built Butler for the Alexa+ track: an add-on that handles real situations for you, keeps a receipt for every action, and turns your corrections into rules the AI can't break.
It's running on an Echo Show 8 in our open-source simulator, against the live stack on AWS. The Black Box on the right records every gateway decision.
I don't give Butler commands. I tell it what's happening.
It plans, and starts on everything it's allowed to do.
Butler never interrupts. It waits until I ask.
One decision is mine, so I'll tap it.
That tap runs under a separate approval identity, not the AI.
Every action has a receipt.
What it used, what it turned down, and the rule that allowed it.
The AI only picks a rule template. Plain code compiles it to Cedar and loads it into AgentCore Policy. It's live at the gateway.
Butler tried to buy drinks for my parents. The gateway denied it, outside the model, before anything was bought.
So it asks instead.
And it flags its own decisions I might disagree with.
Butler runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, Gateway and Policy. Thanks for watching!
